questions.question: What does interoperability allow IoT devices to do?
questions.explanation: Interoperability enables different IoT devices and systems to communicate and exchange data.
questions.source: See Lecture 21 (Interoperability in Internet of Things) @ 03:30

questions.question: Syntactic interoperability deals with:
questions.explanation: Syntactic interoperability concerns the format of messages exchanged between devices and users.
questions.source: See Lecture 21 (Interoperability in Internet of Things) @ 17:01

questions.question: What does UMB stand for?
questions.explanation: UMB stands for Universal Middleware Bridge. It helps different middleware-based devices work together.
questions.source: See Lecture 21 (Interoperability in Internet of Things) @ 25:42

questions.question: What is the operating voltage of the Arduino UNO?
questions.explanation: The Arduino UNO operates at 5 volts.
questions.source: See Lecture 22: Introduction to Arduino Programming – Part I @ 06:57.

questions.question: What is a program written in the Arduino IDE called?
questions.explanation: A program created and uploaded using the Arduino IDE is called a sketch.
questions.source: See Lecture 22 (Introduction to Arduino Programming - Part I) @ 12:12

questions.question: Which interface is mainly used to connect an Arduino UNO to a computer?
questions.explanation: The Arduino UNO uses a USB interface to connect to a computer. The USB connection can be used to upload programs to the board and also provide power during development.
questions.source: See Lecture 22: Introduction to Arduino Programming – Part I @ 07:26

questions.question: What is the conventional starting index of an array in Arduino programming?
questions.explanation: As in C and C++, Arduino arrays use zero-based indexing. Therefore, the first element is stored at index 0.
questions.source: See Lecture 23 (Introduction to Arduino Programming - Part II) @ 04:08

questions.question: Which Arduino function is used to generate a pseudo-random number within a specified range?
questions.explanation: The random() function generates a pseudo-random number in a specified range. For example, random(max) produces a value within the range defined by max.
questions.source: See Lecture 23 (Introduction to Arduino Programming - Part II) @ 09:19

questions.question: In the traffic-control example, which LED is switched ON first to represent the GO signal?
questions.explanation: The traffic() function first sets the green LED HIGH and displays the GO message. After a delay, it switches to yellow and then red.
questions.source: See Lecture 23 (Introduction to Arduino Programming - Part II) @ 14:34

questions.question: Which quantities are measured by a DHT sensor?
questions.explanation: A DHT sensor measures the temperature and humidity of its surroundings.
questions.source: See Lecture 24: Integration of Sensors and Actuators with Arduino – Part I @ 04:37.

questions.question: What does a sensor convert a physical quantity into?
questions.explanation: A sensor is an electronic element that converts a physical quantity or measurement into an electrical signal.
questions.source: See Lecture 24: Integration of Sensors and Actuators with Arduino – Part I, Sensors section.

questions.question: In the DHT sensor sketch, delay(2000) causes successive readings to be printed after approximately how much time?
questions.explanation: The delay() function takes time in milliseconds. Therefore, delay(2000) introduces a delay of 2000 milliseconds, which equals 2 seconds.
questions.source: See Lecture 24 (Integration of Sensors and Actuators with Arduino - Part I) @ 13:34

questions.question: State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: A servo motor is a low-precision motor used only for linear motion.
questions.explanation: A servo motor is a high-precision motor that provides controlled rotary motion.
questions.source: See Lecture 25: Integration of Sensors and Actuators with Arduino – Part II @ 04:30.

questions.question: Which device provides controlled rotary motion?
questions.explanation: A servo motor is an actuator that provides precise and controlled rotary motion.
questions.source: See Lecture 25: Integration of Sensors and Actuators with Arduino – Part II @ 04:30.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: A stepper motor is a type of actuator.
questions.explanation: A stepper motor is one of the motor actuators discussed in the lecture. Other examples include servo motors, hydraulic motors, solenoids, relays, and AC motors.
questions.source: See Lecture 25: Integration of Sensors and Actuators with Arduino – Part II @ 03:20.
